clusters.label: User and Accommodation Reviews

duplicates.reason: These requirements all state that a user (guest/student) can leave a review/feedback for an accommodation (room).
These requirements all state that a host can leave a review/feedback for a guest (student/user).
These are high-level requirements stating that both parties can/should leave reviews after a stay, encompassing the more specific requirements.
Both requirements state that users can view reviews/feedback associated with a listing/room.
These requirements all state that users can view the feedback/reviews received by other users.
These are identical, general requirements stating that users can view feedback/reviews.

inconsistencies.reason: R86 implies feedback can only be left for stays of 'one week', while R250 allows feedback 'after the stay is completed' regardless of duration. This creates a conflict for stays shorter or longer than one week.

ambiguities.issue: The phrase 'At the end of the stay for one week' is highly ambiguous. It could mean the stay must be exactly one week long, or it could be a time window of one week in which to leave a review.
ambiguities.suggestion: Clarify the condition. For example: 'For stays of any duration, users have a one-week window after the stay concludes to leave feedback.'

ambiguities.issue: The 'star rating' is not defined.
ambiguities.suggestion: Specify the scale for the star rating, for example, 'a star rating on a scale of 1 to 5'.

ambiguities.issue: The phrase 'viewing of all feedback related to all users' for a specific bed is nonsensical.
ambiguities.suggestion: Rephrase to clarify the intent, likely: 'The system must allow the viewing of all feedback left for a specific bed by users who have stayed there.'

ambiguities.issue: The term 'manage the average rating' is vague.
ambiguities.suggestion: Specify the action, for example, 'The system must automatically calculate and display the average rating...'

gaps.description: There is no requirement defining how the average ratings mentioned in R146 and R147 are calculated from the individual star ratings defined in R203.
R38 allows users to edit reviews, but there are no rules defined for this process, such as time limits, whether the rating can be changed, or if an edit history is maintained.
The system requests feedback (R178) but does not specify a time window within which a review must be submitted after a stay concludes.

dependencies.reason: Calculating an average room rating (R146) requires that reviews include a quantifiable rating, as specified in R203.
Calculating an average user rating (R147) requires that reviews include a quantifiable rating, as specified in R203.
The ability to edit a review (R38) presupposes that a review has already been created (e.g., via R161).

clusters.quality_reason: The cluster is largely coherent, focusing on reviews and feedback. However, it includes several requirements about publishing accommodations (e.g., 96, 97, 200) and notifications (176, 177) that are contextually related but dilute the primary topic.
clusters.summary: This cluster defines the system's functionality for creating, viewing, editing, and managing reviews and ratings for both users and accommodations.

clusters.label: Purchasing In-App Points

duplicates.reason: All these requirements describe the same core functionality: allowing a user to purchase points. They differ only in minor details like using 'real money' or an 'in-app shop'.
Both requirements specify that points can be purchased using a credit or debit card.

inconsistencies.reason: R134 states a 10% commission on 'point purchases', while R139 states a 1% commission on 'package purchases'. It's unclear if a package purchase is a type of point purchase, making the commission rate contradictory.

ambiguities.issue: The phrase 'retains 10% of the points' is ambiguous. It's unclear if a user buying 100 points receives only 90, or if the system's commission is a monetary value equivalent to 10% of the purchase price.
ambiguities.suggestion: Clarify the commission mechanism, e.g., 'For every point purchase, the system charges a monetary fee equivalent to 10% of the transaction value.'

ambiguities.issue: R138 specifies packages of 50, 100, 150 points, while R136 allows purchases of 'at least 20 points'. It is unclear if users can buy custom amounts (e.g., 25 points) or are restricted to the packages.
ambiguities.suggestion: Specify whether only predefined packages can be purchased or if custom amounts above the minimum are allowed.

gaps.description: The cost of points in real currency is never defined. There is no requirement specifying the price for a point or a package of points.
There are no requirements for handling failed payment transactions, such as displaying an error message to the user or allowing them to retry the purchase.

dependencies.reason: The 1% commission on package purchases (R139) is only applicable if packages, as defined in R138, exist.

clusters.quality_reason: The cluster is highly coherent, with all requirements focusing exclusively on the function of purchasing points.
clusters.summary: This cluster specifies the requirements for users to purchase in-app points using real money, including purchase amounts, payment methods, and system commissions.

clusters.label: Accommodation Listing Creation

duplicates.reason: Both requirements define the necessary information for a listing. R240 is a superset of R199, adding 'photos' and 'city'.
All three requirements contain the same stipulation: the host must provide an availability period for the listing.
These requirements all concern 'add-ons' like sheets and towels. R224 is the general capability, R99 names the items, and R201/R241 describe their impact on price.

ambiguities.issue: The term 'a different price' is not specific enough.
ambiguities.suggestion: Define how the price difference is determined, e.g., 'allow the host to set a fixed additional point cost for providing sheets and/or towels'.

ambiguities.issue: The term 'add-ons' is vague beyond the specified sheets and towels.
ambiguities.suggestion: Specify if the list of add-ons is fixed (e.g., only sheets and towels) or if hosts can define custom add-ons.

gaps.description: While multiple pieces of information for a listing are mentioned (cost, address, photos), it is not specified which of these are mandatory for a listing to be published.
The cluster defines how to create a listing but lacks any requirements for editing or deleting a listing after it has been published.

dependencies.reason: Sending a booking request (R243) is only possible for a published offer, which must be created according to the details in R240.
Applying additional costs for sheets and towels (R241) requires the ability to add them as comforts in the first place (R99).

clusters.quality_reason: The cluster is very coherent, with nearly all requirements focused on the creation and definition of an accommodation listing. The inclusion of R243 (sending a booking request) is the only minor deviation from this theme.
clusters.summary: This cluster details the requirements for hosts to create and define accommodation listings, including mandatory details, optional add-ons, and preventing double-bookings.

clusters.label: Point Transaction for Stays

duplicates.reason: All these requirements state the same rule: the system retains a 10% commission from the points transacted for a stay.
Both requirements specify that the host receives 90% of the points paid for the stay, which is a direct consequence of the 10% commission.

inconsistencies.reason: These requirements specify three conflicting times for payment processing: R245 states it's 'upon host confirmation', R79 states it's at '12:00 PM on the day before check-in', and R133 states it's 'five hours before the start of the stay'. They cannot all be true.

R137 specifies a 2% commission on 'single purchases', while R169 (and many others) specifies a 10% commission on points spent for a service. If a booking is a 'single purchase', these rates are contradictory.

ambiguities.issue: The method for calculating the 'total price in points' is not defined.
ambiguities.suggestion: Specify the formula, e.g., 'Total price is calculated as (points per night * number of nights) + any additional costs for extras.'

ambiguities.issue: The term 'single purchases' is undefined, making it impossible to know when the 2% commission applies.
ambiguities.suggestion: Define 'single purchase' or remove the requirement if it is redundant with other commission rules.

ambiguities.issue: The phrase 'service includes any extras in the fields' is extremely vague.
ambiguities.suggestion: Specify what 'extras' and 'fields' refer to, or remove the requirement if it is not actionable.

gaps.description: R81 specifies that a booking is cancelled if the user cannot pay. However, there is no requirement to notify the guest or the host about this automatic cancellation.
The system processes payments, but there is no requirement for a transaction log or history that would be visible to the user.

dependencies.reason: The condition of being unable to pay (R81) must be checked before the system attempts to subtract points (R80), blocking the transaction if the condition is met.
The amount the host receives (90% in R82) is a direct result of the commission the system deducts (10% in R83).

clusters.quality_reason: The cluster is highly focused on the point transaction process for bookings.
clusters.summary: This cluster defines the financial logic for accommodation bookings, including the timing of payment, deduction of points from guests, crediting points to hosts, and the system's commission structure.

clusters.label: System Validation and Constraints

duplicates.reason: All these requirements enforce the rule that user registration is tied to a valid university email, describing the same constraint from different perspectives (accepting, verifying, rejecting).

ambiguities.issue: The method to 'verify the reachability of the accommodation' is undefined.
ambiguities.suggestion: Specify the verification method, e.g., 'The system must validate the address format and display its location on an integrated map.'

ambiguities.issue: The condition 'If the booking request is valid' is ambiguous because the full set of validity criteria is not defined in one place.
ambiguities.suggestion: Consolidate all booking validation rules or reference them, e.g., 'A booking request is valid if the user has sufficient points (R131) and meets the location criteria (R185).'

ambiguities.issue: The term 'verify the origin of the tenant' is vague.
ambiguities.suggestion: Clarify what 'origin' refers to, such as 'verify the student's home university'.

gaps.description: R185 requires checking that a student is not booking in their own university city. This implies the system must know each student's university and each listing's city, but there are no requirements on how this data is captured, stored, or maintained.
Several requirements (95, 98, 222) prevent publishing an incomplete accommodation listing. However, there is no requirement specifying the user-facing error feedback when this occurs.

R62 mentions a 'university authentication system' and a 'token', implying an external integration (like SSO). The technical requirements for this integration (e.g., protocol, data exchange format) are completely missing.

dependencies.reason: A booking request can only be considered valid (R70) if the check for sufficient points (R131) passes.
A booking request can only be considered valid (R70) if the check on the accommodation's location (R185) passes.

clusters.quality_reason: The cluster's theme of 'validation' is very broad, mixing user identity verification, listing content validation, and booking business rules. This lack of a sharp focus makes the grouping feel like a miscellaneous collection of constraints.
clusters.summary: This cluster groups various validation rules and constraints the system must enforce, covering user registration, accommodation publishing, and booking requests.

clusters.label: Listing Creation and Search

duplicates.reason: These requirements are all semantic duplicates for the core functionality of a user creating or publishing a listing for an accommodation.
Both requirements state that the owner of a listing can modify it.
These requirements all describe the need for a search mechanism for users to find listings.
These requirements all describe search filtering. They overlap significantly on criteria like city/location and dates/period, though the complete list of filters is inconsistent across them.

ambiguities.issue: The requirement to 'keep track of the search history' is underspecified.
ambiguities.suggestion: Define the scope of the history, such as its duration (e.g., session-only or persistent) and whether the user can clear it.

ambiguities.issue: The requirement for a 'chat' is too general.
ambiguities.suggestion: Specify the minimum required features for the messaging system, such as text-only messages, timestamps, and read status.

ambiguities.issue: The filter parameter 'requested services' is undefined.
ambiguities.suggestion: Specify what services can be filtered on or link to a definition of available services.

gaps.description: The requirements for search (e.g., R148) do not specify how search results should be sorted by default (e.g., by date, price, relevance) or if the user can change the sort order.
While there are requirements to create (R157) and modify (R158) a listing, there is no corresponding requirement to delete a listing.
R158 allows a listing to be modified, but there is no requirement defining the system's behavior if a listing with pending booking requests is changed.

dependencies.reason: The ability to have search filters (R149) depends on the existence of a search bar or engine (R148).
Modifying a bed (R65) can only happen after a bed has been registered (R63).

clusters.quality_reason: The cluster is reasonably coherent but combines two distinct functional areas: managing one's own listings and searching for others' listings.
clusters.summary: This cluster covers the lifecycle of an accommodation listing, including its creation, modification, and the user's ability to search, filter, and save listings.

clusters.label: Maximum Stay Duration Constraint

duplicates.reason: All of these requirements define the exact same business rule: a stay cannot be longer than 7 nights. They use slightly different wording ('less than 8 days', 'up to 7 nights', 'exceeds 7 days') but are semantically identical.

ambiguities.issue: The interchangeable use of 'days' (R116, R186) and 'nights' (R40, R170, R223, R239, R7) can lead to off-by-one errors.
ambiguities.suggestion: Standardize on one unit, preferably 'nights', as it is less ambiguous for accommodation bookings. For example: 'The number of nights for a single booking cannot exceed 7.'

gaps.description: When a user attempts to book a stay longer than the allowed duration, the system 'prevents' or 'rejects' it, but there is no requirement for providing specific user-facing feedback or an error message explaining why.

clusters.quality_reason: The cluster is extremely coherent as it focuses on a single business rule. The score is lowered due to the high level of redundancy and the inclusion of one unrelated requirement (R215 on point balances).
clusters.summary: This cluster defines a single, repeated business rule that limits the maximum duration of any accommodation booking to seven nights.

clusters.label: Points Economy Management

duplicates.reason: All these requirements state that a user receives a point bonus upon registration. They are inconsistent on the amount (50 vs 100 vs N).
These are identical requirements stating that a user must be able to view their points balance.
These are identical requirements prohibiting users from selling points to each other.
Both requirements specify that the host receives 90% of the points from a booking.

inconsistencies.reason: R2 specifies an initial balance of 100 points upon registration, while R60 specifies 50 points for the same event. These amounts are contradictory.

R122 states points are NOT deducted 'at the moment of booking', while R225 states points ARE transferred 'once the booking is made'. These appear to be contradictory instructions for the same point in time.
R85 states that the system 'does not provide refunds' if payment has occurred. R218 explicitly defines a refund policy (80% of points). These are in direct logical contradiction.
R217 implies a full refund ('refund the requesting student the points spent'), while R218 specifies a partial refund ('return 80% of the points spent').

ambiguities.issue: The threshold for 'running low on points' is not defined.
ambiguities.suggestion: Specify a concrete number or a configurable percentage for when the notification should be triggered.

ambiguities.issue: The requirement to 'give N free points' is ambiguous because 'N' is an undefined variable.
ambiguities.suggestion: Replace 'N' with a specific number of points to be awarded.

ambiguities.issue: The term 'appropriate additional cost' is subjective and vague.
ambiguities.suggestion: Specify how the cost is determined, e.g., 'allow the host to set the additional cost in points'.

gaps.description: The system manages a points economy, but there is no requirement for an administrative function to manually adjust a user's point balance to correct errors or for customer support reasons.
R182 requires a point transaction history, but it does not specify a retention policy for how long this history should be stored and accessible to the user.

dependencies.reason: The system must ensure a student has enough points (R30) before it can subtract points for a booking (R48).
The no-refund policy of R85 would block the refund action specified in R217 from ever occurring after payment.

clusters.quality_reason: The cluster is thematically coherent around the 'points economy'.
clusters.summary: This cluster defines the entire economy of the in-app currency 'points,' including how they are created, distributed, earned, spent, and the rules governing their use.

clusters.label: User Account and Profile Management

duplicates.reason: These are all identical requirements stating that the system must allow users/students to register.
All these requirements specify the same constraint: registration must be done using a university email address.
These requirements all describe the same user flow: redirecting the user to their university's external authentication page.
Both requirements state the need for a user-to-user messaging feature.

ambiguities.issue: It is unclear what 'information related to the user' the system will receive from the university.
ambiguities.suggestion: Specify the exact data fields to be received, e.g., 'first name, last name, and verified email address'.

ambiguities.issue: The process for handling a user report for 'inappropriate behavior' is completely undefined.
ambiguities.suggestion: Define what happens after a report is submitted: who reviews it, what actions can be taken (e.g., warning, suspension), and if the reporter receives feedback.

ambiguities.issue: The term 'wallet' is not defined in this context.
ambiguities.suggestion: Clarify if 'wallet' simply refers to the user's point balance or if it implies a more complex feature for managing different assets.

gaps.description: The cluster covers user registration and logout (R109), but there are no requirements for password management, such as a 'forgot password' or 'reset password' feature.
While R179 and R93 define the content of a user profile, there is no requirement that allows a user to edit their profile information after registration.
The system includes notifications (R73, R174), but there is no requirement for user-configurable notification preferences (e.g., to enable or disable specific notification types).

dependencies.reason: Receiving user information from the university (R113) can only happen after the user has been redirected to and successfully authenticated with the university's service (R111).

clusters.quality_reason: The cluster is thematically strong, focusing on user accounts, profiles, and core interactions. While it covers several topics (registration, profiles, messaging), they are all tightly related to user management.
clusters.summary: This cluster focuses on user lifecycle management, including registration and authentication via university systems, user profiles, and core communication features.

clusters.label: Booking and Accommodation Lifecycle

duplicates.reason: These are all semantic duplicates for the core user action of booking or requesting to book an accommodation.
All these requirements describe the host's ability to manage booking requests. R126 ('view, approve, and reject') is a superset of the others, which describe the individual actions.
These requirements are identical, stating that a user can cancel a submitted booking or request.

These requirements concern updating accommodation availability. R77 is the most comprehensive, covering acceptance and cancellation, while R127 is a specific case (rejection) and R124 is a general statement.

ambiguities.issue: The term 'periodically verify' is not defined, and the consequences of a user no longer being an active student are not specified.
ambiguities.suggestion: Define the verification frequency (e.g., 'annually') and the actions to be taken upon failure (e.g., 'deactivate the account and cancel future bookings').

ambiguities.issue: The requirement to 'redeem gift cards with points' is completely undefined and appears unrelated to the cluster's topic.
ambiguities.suggestion: Elaborate on the gift card feature in a separate, dedicated requirement set, or remove this requirement if it is out of scope.

ambiguities.issue: It is unclear what makes a booking request 'invalid' or how the system would 'request modifications'.
ambiguities.suggestion: Define the criteria for an invalid request and specify the user-facing mechanism for requesting changes.

gaps.description: R110 allows a user to delete their account, but there are no requirements defining what happens to their future bookings (both as a guest and a host) or their existing listings upon account deletion.
There is no time limit specified for a host to accept or reject a booking request before it might automatically expire.
R19 allows a student to delete their room, but the consequences for any existing future bookings for that room are not defined.

dependencies.reason: Automatically rejecting other requests (R75) is triggered only after the owner accepts one specific request (R74).
Making an accommodation available again (R127) is a consequence of the host rejecting a booking (an action described in R126).

clusters.quality_reason: This cluster has very low coherence. It acts as a 'catch-all' for many different features, including booking, account deletion, listing management, and even review management. The inclusion of the completely unrelated gift card requirement (R228) highlights the lack of a clear focus.
clusters.summary: This cluster describes the end-to-end process of booking and managing accommodations, including guest actions like requesting and cancelling, and host actions like approving or rejecting requests.
